requirements_summary: Workload: agent assist for L2 agents + automated tool-calling to create/update tickets in HelixService and trigger refunds via Stripe/Payments API
Latency target for assist suggestions: median < 120ms, p95 < 400ms during normal load
Tool-calling SLO: acknowledgment from backend within 1s for create/update calls; compensating transactions acceptable for refunds with idempotency
Throughput target: baseline 200 reqs/sec, burst 1,500 reqs/sec during campaign peaks (Black Friday style)
Cost sensitivity: mid-high; looking to trade slightly higher latency for lower token-unit cost for bulk summarization
Model preferences: fine with open-model variants; want quantization/throughput guidance; must support structured tool call outputs (JSON) and schema validation
Routing/fallback: prefer hosted primary with dedicated fallback during spikes; want automatic routing by region and model-variant for cost control
Security/compliance: SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, audit logging for tool calls, envelope encryption for PII, optional data residency in us-east-1
notes: Customer quote: 'We need the assist to feel invisible — no extra clicks, accurate ticket mutations, guarantees around refunds.'

POC success criteria: 1) accurate ticket create/update rate > 98% across 1,000 synthetic interactions; 2) refund calls succeed and are idempotent; 3) p95 latency within target during 5-minute burst test
Security review: already provided SOC2 report and encryption architecture; legal pushed back on payment flow — require PCI scoping decision
Engineering ask: webhook adapter for HelixService requires path-based retry + dedupe token; Rafael to pair with Helix infra on 2026-03-16
Notes from demo: showed tool-calling flow that returned 'ticket_id' and 'escalation_required' flag; customer liked structured outputs and function call reliability
Risk: Helix does refunds via a separate financial microservice with stricter rate limits (10 TPS) — Redwood must support throttling and queued compensating actions
Suggested Redwood features: automated rate-limit shaping per downstream API, built-in retry/backoff policies, and canned content transforms for HelixService payloads
